_notes: THE ROCK ATLAS -- eight stills, one per cell, NOT a sequence: the emitter
picks one per particle by hash, so the folder is a palette.
EXPLICIT RECTS, the README's own boundaries, same 1774x887 4x2 delivery as
the rest of the pack.
WHAT EACH CELL IS, and this is the one atlas in the pack where it matters:
c0-c5 are six individual rock chunks of visibly INCREASING size and ink
coverage (c0 10.1% up to c2's 34.3%) -- small pebble through a fist-sized
boulder fragment. c6 is a scattered grit cluster (several small chips, not
one shape). c7 is a soft dust puff, diffuse rather than solid.
THE README'S OWN WARNING: 'avoid uniformly random selection across all
eight if it produces oversized dust or too many heavy chunks.' Named here
because it could not be resolved in content -- see the report's headline
finding. SpellEmitter's frame pick is one hash mod frameCount
(SpellEmitterSim.At, channel 6) with no per-cell weight field, so every one
of these eight -- pebble through boulder through soft dust puff -- is equally
likely per particle, and the same sizeMin/sizeMax range in skills.json scales
all eight identically even though their own ink footprints differ by more
than 3x. Kept as all eight named cells rather than dropping any, because
trimming the palette in the recipe would be quietly overruling the artist's
atlas rather than reporting the gap; skills.json's emitters instead choose a
conservative size range and hold the earth spray's burst count down
(see the vfx block's own commentary).
NO CANVAS STATED: the rects give 444x444/443x443 cells and nothing scales,
so the automatic pad onto the largest cell is sufficient.
Delivered with its own alpha; keyed is false.
